outcome.answer:
Repeating training data can hurt pretraining performance, but the effect depends on how repetition is structured and how much unique data is available [1, 3]. One study finds a systematic loss peak at an intermediate repeat count, with the most damaging repeat count growing with model size, and says repeated documents can waste substantial compute compared with no repetition [1]. Another finds that repetition damage is scale-dependent: limited uniqueness causes only mild degradation for small models but rapidly increasing loss penalties for larger models [3].

Not all repetition is equally bad: one paper reports that, under a fixed update budget, more epochs on smaller datasets can improve downstream results in supervised fine-tuning, with gains saturating at full memorization [6]. Another reports that a second epoch can be worth nearly as much as fresh data, but also that replaying shards consecutively or concentrating repeats on fewer samples raises loss [2].
